The para-isomer dominates primarily because:
options: A) The para-position experiences significantly less steric hindrance between the incoming bulky nitronium group and the existing chlorine atom
B) The inductive electron-withdrawing effect of chlorine is completely absent at the para-position
C) The resonance electron-donating effect operates exclusively at the para-position and not at the ortho-position
D) Nitration at the ortho-position generates an anti-aromatic intermediate
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand directing influence of halogen. Chlorine possesses $+R$ resonance electron donation, which selectively increases electron density at both ortho and para positions relative to meta positions. Therefore, electrophilic nitration by the nitronium ion ($\text{NO}_2^+$) occurs at the ortho and para positions.
Step 2: Compare ortho vs para attack. The chlorine atom is a relatively large atom with high electron density. Attack of the electrophile at the adjacent ortho position experiences substantial steric repulsion and electrostatic clash with the chlorine substituent. In contrast, the para position is diametrically opposite and completely unhindered sterically.
Step 3: Conclude the product ratio: Due to minimal steric hindrance, the para-isomer (1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene) is formed as the major product ($70\%$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An alkyl halide $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{11}\text{Br}$ (Compound A) reacts with magnesium metal in dry ether to form a Grignard reagent (Compound B). When Compound B is treated with heavy water ($\text{D}_2\text{O}$), it gives 2-methylbutane-2-$d$ represented as $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C(D)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$. What is the IUPAC name of Compound A?
options: A) 1-Bromo-2-methylbutane
B) 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane
C) 2-Bromo-3-methylbutane
D) 1-Bromo-3-methylbutane
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Write the general Grignard reaction with heavy water: $\text{R}-\text{MgBr} + \text{D}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{R}-\text{D} + \text{Mg(OD)Br}$.
Step 2: Identify the position of deuterium. The product formed is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C(D)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$, which has deuterium attached directly to carbon-2 of the 2-methylbutane skeleton.
Step 3: Deduce the alkyl group. The carbon atom attached to deuterium (C2) must be the exact carbon that was bonded to magnesium in the Grignard reagent, which in turn was the carbon bonded to bromine in Compound A. Thus, Compound A must be 2-bromo-2-methylbutane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements labeled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Allyl chloride ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$) undergoes nucleophilic substitution reactions much more readily than vinyl chloride ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{Cl}$).
Reason (R): In allyl chloride, heterolytic cleavage of the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond yields a carbocation stabilized by resonance across the adjacent double bond, whereas in vinyl chloride, the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond has partial double bond character due to resonance and the vinylic cation is highly unstable.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
options: A) (A) is true but (R) is false
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Allyl chloride readily undergoes both $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ and $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ nucleophilic substitution reactions, whereas vinyl chloride is exceptionally inert towards nucleophiles. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). In allyl chloride, ionization gives the allyl carbocation ($[\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2^+ \leftrightarrow ^+\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2]$), which is stabilized by resonance between two equivalent structures. In vinyl chloride, the unshared electron pair of chlorine is conjugated with the double bond ($[\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{Cl} \leftrightarrow ^-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{Cl}^+]$), giving partial double bond character and shortening the bond. Moreover, cleavage of vinyl chloride would produce a vinyl carbocation where the positive charge is localized in an $sp$ orbital, which is energetically very unfavorable. Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: How many monochloro derivatives (including stereoisomers) are theoretically possible from the photochemical free-radical monochlorination of 2-methylbutane?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify all constitutionally isomeric monochloro derivatives of 2-methylbutane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$):
1. 1-Chloro-2-methylbutane: $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$
2. 2-Chloro-2-methylbutane: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C(Cl)}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$
3. 2-Chloro-3-methylbutane: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH(Cl)}-\text{CH}_3$
4. 1-Chloro-3-methylbutane: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$
Step 2: Determine chirality for each isomer:
- In 1-chloro-2-methylbutane, C2 is bonded to $-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, $-\text{H}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, and $-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$. It is a chiral center, giving a pair of enantiomers ($2$ stereoisomers: $R$ and $S$).
- In 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, C2 has two identical methyl groups; it is achiral ($1$ isomer).
- In 2-chloro-3-methylbutane, C2 is bonded to $-\text{H}$, $-\text{Cl}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, and an isopropyl group. It has a chiral center, giving a pair of enantiomers ($2$ stereoisomers: $R$ and $S$).
- In 1-chloro-3-methylbutane, no carbon has four different groups; it is achiral ($1$ isomer).
Step 3: Sum total stereoisomers: $2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 6$ stereoisomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding chlorofluorocarbons (Freons):
(I) Freon-12 (dichlorodifluoromethane, $\text{CCl}_2\text{F}_2$) is manufactured industrially from tetrachloromethane by the Swarts reaction using antimony trifluoride in the presence of antimony pentachloride.
(II) Freons are extremely stable, unreactive, non-toxic, non-corrosive, and easily liquefiable gases.
(III) In the stratosphere, Freon-12 undergoes photochemical homolysis by ultraviolet radiation to release chlorine free radicals that catalytically destroy ozone molecules.
Which of the above statements are correct according to NCERT?
options: A) (I), (II), and (III)
B) (I) and (II) only
C) (II) and (III) only
D) (I) and (III) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate statement (I). Freon-12 ($\text{CCl}_2\text{F}_2$) is one of the most common chlorofluorocarbons and is manufactured from $\text{CCl}_4$ by the Swarts reaction: $3\text{CCl}_4 + 2\text{SbF}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{SbCl}_5} 3\text{CCl}_2\text{F}_2 + 2\text{SbCl}_3$. Statement (I) is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate statement (II). NCERT explicitly describes Freons as extremely stable, unreactive, non-toxic, non-corrosive, and easily liquefiable gases, which led to their widespread use as refrigerants and aerosol propellants. Statement (II) is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate statement (III). In the stratosphere, intense UV radiation initiates homolytic fission of $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bonds in freons: $\text{CF}_2\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} ^\bullet\text{CF}_2\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}^\bullet$. The chlorine radical reacts with ozone: $\text{Cl}^\bullet + \text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{ClO}^\bullet + \text{O}_2$, and $\text{ClO}^\bullet + \text{O} \rightarrow \text{Cl}^\bullet + \text{O}_2$. A single chlorine radical can destroy up to $100{,}000$ ozone molecules. Statement (III) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{HBr, benzoyl peroxide}} \text{Compound A} \xrightarrow{\text{AgCN (alc.)}} \text{Compound B} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{Compound C}$
What is the correct IUPAC name of Compound C?
options: A) Butan-1-amine
B) $N$-Methylpropan-1-amine
C) $N,N$-Dimethylpropan-1-amine
D) 2-Methylpropan-1-amine
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify Compound A. Addition of $\text{HBr}$ to propene in the presence of benzoyl peroxide proceeds via the anti-Markovnikov free-radical pathway to give 1-bromopropane: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$.
Step 2: Identify Compound B. Reaction of 1-bromopropane with silver cyanide ($\text{AgCN}$), a covalent reagent, results in nucleophilic attack through the lone pair of the nitrogen atom to form an alkyl isocyanide: propyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{NC}$).
Step 3: Identify Compound C. Reduction of an alkyl isocyanide with lithium aluminium hydride ($\text{LiAlH}_4$) reduces the isonitrile group into a secondary amine containing an $N$-methyl group: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_3$. The IUPAC name is $N$-methylpropan-1-amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following haloalkanes, upon alkaline hydrolysis with aqueous sodium hydroxide followed by treatment with iodine ($\text{I}_2$) in alkaline medium, produces a yellow precipitate of triiodomethane (iodoform)?
options: A) 3-Chloropentane
B) 1-Chlorobutane
C) 2-Chlorobutane
D) 1-Chloropropane
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the iodoform test requirement. The haloform/iodoform reaction requires compounds containing either the $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}=\text{O}$ group or the $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, which can be oxidized by hypoiodite ($\text{OI}^-$) to a methyl ketone.
Step 2: Determine the hydrolysis product of each haloalkane:
- Alkaline hydrolysis of 2-chlorobutane gives butan-2-ol ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$), which contains the $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit.
- Alkaline hydrolysis of 1-chlorobutane gives butan-1-ol (primary alcohol, no $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit).
- Alkaline hydrolysis of 3-chloropentane gives pentan-3-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, no methyl group directly attached to the carbinol carbon).
- Alkaline hydrolysis of 1-chloropropane gives propan-1-ol (primary alcohol).
Step 3: Conclude the positive test: Butan-2-ol from 2-chlorobutane is oxidized to butan-2-one and then iodinated and cleaved to form a yellow crystalline precipitate of iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the organochlorine insecticide DDT ($p,p'$-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane):
Statement I: DDT is prepared commercially by the condensation of chloral (trichloroethanal, $\text{CCl}_3\text{CHO}$) with chlorobenzene in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid.
Statement II: DDT is highly water-soluble and rapidly metabolized and excreted by animals, which is why it poses no bioaccumulation hazards.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:
options: A) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
D) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. DDT is synthesized by condensing one molecule of chloral with two molecules of chlorobenzene in the presence of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ as a dehydrating agent: $\text{CCl}_3\text{CHO} + 2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4} (p\text{-Cl}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4)_2\text{CH}-\text{CCl}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. DDT has extremely low water solubility and high lipid solubility. Because of its chemical stability and lipid affinity, it is not rapidly metabolized or excreted; instead, it accumulates in the fatty tissues of animals. This leads to biomagnification along food chains, causing serious reproductive and ecological damage (such as eggshell thinning in birds of prey), leading to its global ban. Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match the inorganic reagents reacting with haloalkane ($\text{R}-\text{X}$) in List I with the primary functional group class of the organic product in List II:
List I:
(P) $\text{KCN}$ in aqueous alcohol
(Q) $\text{AgCN}$ in aqueous alcohol
(R) $\text{KNO}_2$ in aqueous alcohol
(S) $\text{AgNO}_2$ in aqueous alcohol

List II:
(1) Nitroalkane ($\text{R}-\text{NO}_2$)
(2) Alkyl isocyanide (carbylamine, $\text{R}-\text{NC}$)
(3) Alkyl nitrite ($\text{R}-\text{O}-\text{N}=\text{O}$)
(4) Alkyl cyanide (nitrile, $\text{R}-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$)

Choose the correct match from the options below:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match (P) $\text{KCN}$. $\text{KCN}$ is ionic and provides cyanide ion ($[:\text{C}\equiv\text{N}:]^-$). Attack occurs predominantly through carbon to yield an alkyl cyanide (nitrile, $\text{R}-\text{CN}$). Thus, $\text{P} \rightarrow 4$.
Step 2: Match (Q) $\text{AgCN}$. $\text{AgCN}$ is covalent and attack takes place through the lone pair of electrons on nitrogen, yielding an alkyl isocyanide (isocyanide, $\text{R}-\text{NC}$). Thus, $\text{Q} \rightarrow 2$.
Step 3: Match (R) $\text{KNO}_2$. $\text{KNO}_2$ is ionic and provides nitrite ion ($[\text{O}-\text{N}=\text{O}]^-$). The negative charge on oxygen attacks the alkyl carbon, producing an alkyl nitrite ($\text{R}-\text{O}-\text{N}=\text{O}$). Thus, $\text{R} \rightarrow 3$.
Step 4: Match (S) $\text{AgNO}_2$. $\text{AgNO}_2$ is predominantly covalent; the nitrogen lone pair attacks the alkyl carbon, resulting in a nitroalkane ($\text{R}-\text{NO}_2$). Thus, $\text{S} \rightarrow 1$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When 2-bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane is heated with aqueous ethanol in the absence of a strong base, the major solvolysis substitution product obtained is:
options: A) 2-Ethoxy-3,3-dimethylbutane
B) 2-Ethoxy-2,3-dimethylbutane
C) 3,3-Dimethylbutan-2-ol
D) 1-Ethoxy-3,3-dimethylbutane
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the mechanism. Heating with a neutral polar protic solvent (aqueous ethanol) without a strong base promotes solvolysis via the unimolecular $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway.
Step 2: Trace carbocation formation and rearrangement. Heterolytic departure of the bromide ion from 2-bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH(Br)}-\text{CH}_3$) generates an initial secondary carbocation: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}^+-\text{CH}_3$. To relieve angle strain and achieve greater electronic stability, a 1,2-methyl shift occurs from the adjacent quaternary carbon. This transforms the less stable secondary carbocation into a significantly more stable tertiary carbocation: $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}^+-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$.
Step 3: Determine the product. Nucleophilic capture of this rearranged tertiary carbocation by ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) followed by proton loss produces 2-ethoxy-2,3-dimethylbutane as the predominant substitution product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In bimolecular $\text{E}2$ dehydrohalogenation reactions, elimination requires an anti-periplanar conformation between the $\beta$-hydrogen and the leaving halogen. Treatment of $(1R,2S)$-1-chloro-1,2-diphenylpropane with sodium ethoxide in ethanol predominantly yields:
options: A) 3,3-Diphenylprop-1-ene
B) $(E)$-1,2-Diphenylprop-1-ene
C) $(Z)$-1,2-Diphenylprop-1-ene
D) 1,2-Diphenylprop-2-ene
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the stereoelectronic requirement of the $\text{E}2$ mechanism. For orbital overlap to smoothly convert $sp^3$ hybrid orbitals into the newly forming $\pi$ bond, the $\text{C}_\beta-\text{H}$ bond and the $\text{C}_\alpha-\text{Cl}$ bond must lie in the same plane and point in opposite directions (dihedral angle $= 180^\circ$, anti-periplanar conformation).
Step 2: Draw the Newman projection for $(1R,2S)$-1-chloro-1,2-diphenylpropane. On C1 (front), we have $-\text{Cl}$, $-\text{H}$, and $-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$. On C2 (back), we have $-\text{H}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, and $-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$. Rotating about the $\text{C}_1-\text{C}_2$ single bond to place the $\beta$-hydrogen exactly anti to the leaving chlorine group puts the two bulky phenyl ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$) rings on the same side of the developing double bond.
Step 3: Conclude the alkene geometry. Simultaneous abstraction of the anti-hydrogen by ethoxide and loss of chloride locks the geometry into $(Z)$-1,2-diphenylprop-1-ene as the major stereospecific elimination product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The bridgehead halide 1-bromobicyclo[2.2.1]heptane is exceptionally inert towards both $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ and $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ nucleophilic substitutions. Which of the following provides the correct mechanistic justification?
options: A) The bridgehead carbon is $sp$-hybridized and cannot accommodate incoming electron pairs
B) The carbon-bromine bond has $100\%$ ionic character which prevents nucleophilic displacement
C) The bicyclic cage easily undergoes ring expansion to form an unreactive cyclobutane derivative
D) Inability of the bridgehead carbon to adopt a planar $sp^2$ geometry prevents carbocation formation (Bredt's rule), while the cage structure rigidly blocks backside attack by nucleophiles
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze resistance to the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway. Ionization via $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ requires the bridgehead carbon to become a carbocation. A stable carbocation must attain planar $sp^2$ geometry (bond angles $120^\circ$). In the rigid bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane cage, the bridgehead carbon is constrained to a pyramidal geometry with bond angles constrained near $109.5^\circ$ or smaller, creating intolerable ring strain that forbids planarity. Furthermore, according to Bredt's rule, a bridgehead double bond or planar radical/cation cannot be accommodated in small bicyclic rings.
Step 2: Analyze resistance to the $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ pathway. The $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism requires backside attack at $180^\circ$ relative to the carbon-bromine bond. The rigid bicyclic carbon framework encloses the backside of the bridgehead carbon, making it sterically impossible for any nucleophile to access the reaction center from behind.
Step 3: Conclude why both pathways fail: Bridgehead geometry forbids both planarity for $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ and backside approach for $\text{S}_\text{N}2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following multi-step reaction cascade:
$\text{Toluene} \xrightarrow{3\text{Cl}_2/h\nu, \Delta} \text{Compound A} \xrightarrow{\text{aq. Ca(OH)}_2, \Delta} \text{Compound B} \xrightarrow{\text{PCl}_5} \text{Compound C} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2, \text{Pd-BaSO}_4, \text{quinoline}} \text{Compound D}$
What is the IUPAC name and structure of Compound D?
options: A) Benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$)
B) Benzyl alcohol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$)
C) Acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$)
D) Benzoic acid ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify Compound A. Photochemical chlorination of boiling toluene with excess chlorine ($3\text{Cl}_2/h\nu$) results in complete free-radical chlorination of the benzylic methyl group to form benzotrichloride: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CCl}_3$.
Step 2: Identify Compound B. Hydrolysis of benzotrichloride with aqueous base ($(\text{aq. Ca(OH)}_2)$ or $\text{aq. NaOH}$) replaces the three chlorine atoms with three $-\text{OH}$ groups on the same carbon, which spontaneously loses water to produce benzoic acid: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$.
Step 3: Identify Compound C. Treatment of benzoic acid with $\text{PCl}_5$ yields benzoyl chloride: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl} + \text{POCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$.
Step 4: Identify Compound D. Catalytic hydrogenation of benzoyl chloride using Lindlar-type Rosenmund catalyst ($\text{H}_2$ over $\text{Pd-BaSO}_4$ poisoned with quinoline or sulfur) selectively reduces the acid chloride to benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
The nucleophilic substitution of a secondary alkyl halide $\text{R}-\text{Br}$ in aqueous ethanol proceeds concurrently through both unimolecular and bimolecular pathways according to the total rate law:
$$\text{Rate} = k_1[\text{RBr}] + k_2[\text{RBr}][\text{OH}^-]$$
At initial concentrations $[\text{RBr}] = 0.10\text{ M}$ and $[\text{OH}^-] = 0.10\text{ M}$, the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway accounts for $40\%$ of the total substitution while the $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ pathway accounts for $60\%$. If $[\text{RBr}]$ is doubled to $0.20\text{ M}$ and $[\text{OH}^-]$ is quadrupled to $0.40\text{ M}$, by what factor does the total rate of reaction increase?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Set up the initial rate expressions. Let the initial total rate be $R_0 = 100\text{ units}$.
The initial $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ component is $R_{1,0} = k_1[\text{RBr}]_0 = 40\text{ units}$.
The initial $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ component is $R_{2,0} = k_2[\text{RBr}]_0[\text{OH}^-]_0 = 60\text{ units}$.
Step 2: Determine new rates under altered concentrations. $[\text{RBr}] = 2[\text{RBr}]_0$ and $[\text{OH}^-] = 4[\text{OH}^-]_0$.
- For the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway (first-order in $[\text{RBr}]$, independent of $[\text{OH}^-]$):
$$R_{1,\text{new}} = k_1(2[\text{RBr}]_0) = 2 \times R_{1,0} = 2 \times 40 = 80\text{ units}$$
- For the $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ pathway (first-order in $[\text{RBr}]$ and first-order in $[\text{OH}^-]$):
$$R_{2,\text{new}} = k_2(2[\text{RBr}]_0)(4[\text{OH}^-]_0) = 8 \times R_{2,0} = 8 \times 60 = 480\text{ units}$$
Step 3: Calculate the new total rate and fold change:
$$R_{\text{total, new}} = R_{1,\text{new}} + R_{2,\text{new}} = 80 + 480 = 560\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Factor increase} = \frac{R_{\text{total, new}}}{R_0} = \frac{560}{100} = 5.6$$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding nucleophilic aromatic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$) of activated haloarenes:
Statement I: In the reaction of 1-halo-2,4-dinitrobenzenes with amines, 1-fluoro-2,4-dinitrobenzene reacts dramatically faster than 1-chloro- or 1-bromo-2,4-dinitrobenzene ($-\text{F} \gg -\text{Cl} \approx -\text{Br} \approx -\text{I}$).
Statement II: In the $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$ addition-elimination mechanism, the rate-determining step is the nucleophilic addition to form the Meisenheimer intermediate; the high electronegativity of fluorine strongly stabilizes the negative charge in the transition state, whereas the subsequent loss of halide is fast.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:
options: A) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Sanger's reagent (1-fluoro-2,4-dinitrobenzene) reacts with amino groups hundreds of times faster than 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene ($-\text{F} \gg -\text{Cl} \approx -\text{Br}$). This is opposite to aliphatic nucleophilic substitutions where fluoride is the worst leaving group. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$ mechanism consists of two steps: Step 1 is the addition of the nucleophile to form a cyclohexadienyl anion (Meisenheimer complex), and Step 2 is the expulsion of the halide leaving group. Because aromaticity is lost in Step 1, Step 1 has a high activation barrier and is the slow, rate-determining step. Due to its superior electronegativity, fluorine withdraws electron density most strongly via induction ($-I$), lowering the activation energy for the nucleophile's attack and heavily stabilizing the carbanionic transition state. Carbon-halogen bond cleavage occurs in the second, fast step; hence leaving group ability does not dictate the overall rate. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following chemical reactions performed on optically pure $(S)$-2-bromobutane:
(I) Reaction with sodium iodide ($\text{NaI}$) in dry acetone yielding 2-iodobutane.
(II) Reaction with sodium hydrosulfide ($\text{NaSH}$) in ethanol yielding butan-2-thiol.
(III) Reaction with alcoholic potassium hydroxide ($\text{alc. KOH}$) at elevated temperature yielding but-2-ene.
(IV) Reaction with magnesium in dry ether followed by treatment with water yielding butane.
Which of the following statements correctly identifies the stereochemical outcome of these transformations?
options: A) Reaction (III) yields an optically active $(Z)$-alkene as the major product
B) All four reactions yield products that retain the $(S)$ configuration and remain optically active
C) Reaction (I) yields a racemic mixture while Reaction (II) gives retention of configuration
D) Reactions (I) and (II) proceed with complete inversion of configuration at the stereocenter, while reactions (III) and (IV) yield optically inactive products
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Reaction (I). The Finkelstein reaction of $(S)$-2-bromobutane with $\text{NaI}$ in acetone follows a bimolecular $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism involving backside attack. This leads to complete inversion of configuration, forming $(R)$-2-iodobutane.
Step 2: Analyze Reaction (II). Similarly, the hydrosulfide anion ($\text{SH}^-$) is a powerful, compact nucleophile that displaces bromide via $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ with complete inversion of configuration, forming $(R)$-butan-2-thiol.
Step 3: Analyze Reaction (III). $\beta$-Elimination by alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ predominantly yields but-2-ene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$). But-2-ene lacks an asymmetric carbon and has a plane of symmetry, making it achiral and optically inactive.
Step 4: Analyze Reaction (IV). Formation of the Grignard reagent followed by protonation gives butane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$), which is achiral and optically inactive. Thus, (I) and (II) invert configuration, whereas (III) and (IV) yield optically inactive products.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements labeled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Chlorobenzene does not produce any precipitate of silver chloride ($\text{AgCl}$) when warmed with aqueous silver nitrate solution, whereas benzyl chloride produces an immediate curdy white precipitate.
Reason (R): In chlorobenzene, delocalization of chlorine lone pairs gives the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond partial double bond character and suppresses ionization, whereas benzyl chloride readily ionizes to form a resonance-stabilized benzyl carbocation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Treatment with ethanolic or aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$ is a diagnostic test for ionizable halide ions. Chlorobenzene does not react with $\text{AgNO}_3$ even upon heating, while benzyl chloride forms a white precipitate of $\text{AgCl}$ rapidly. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). In benzyl chloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$), the chlorine is attached to an $sp^3$ benzylic carbon. Heterolytic cleavage is assisted by $\text{Ag}^+$ precipitation to give a benzyl carbocation ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2^+$), which is strongly stabilized by resonance across the aromatic ring. In contrast, in chlorobenzene, the chlorine lone pairs are delocalized into the $\pi$ system ($+R$ resonance), imparting partial double bond character to the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond and making it shorter and much stronger ($169\text{ pm}$ vs $178\text{ pm}$). Furthermore, self-ionization would generate an extremely unstable phenyl cation with a localized vacant $sp^2$ orbital orthogonal to the $\pi$ cloud. Thus, Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match the reaction sequences involving haloalkanes or haloarenes in List I with their corresponding major organic products in List II:
List I:
(P) $\text{Benzene} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{anhyd. AlCl}_3} \text{Product}$
(Q) $\text{Phenol} + \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{NaOH} \xrightarrow{340\text{ K}} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{Product}$
(R) $\text{Chlorobenzene} + \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{Product}$
(S) $\text{Aniline} \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl}, 273-278\text{ K}} \xrightarrow{\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2/\text{HCl}} \text{Product}$

List II:
(1) Chlorobenzene
(2) Toluene
(3) Salicylaldehyde
(4) Isopropylbenzene (cumene)

Choose the correct match from the options below:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match reaction (P). Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with 1-chloropropane in the presence of $\text{anhyd. AlCl}_3$ generates a primary propyl carbocation, which rapidly undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to form the more stable secondary isopropyl carbocation. Electrophilic aromatic attack by this carbocation on benzene gives isopropylbenzene (cumene) as the major product. Thus, $\text{P} \rightarrow 4$.
Step 2: Match reaction (Q). Treatment of phenol with chloroform and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ at $340\text{ K}$ followed by acidification is the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, generating dichlorocarbene (:$!\text{CCl}_2$) as the electrophile to yield salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde). Thus, $\text{Q} \rightarrow 3$.
Step 3: Match reaction (R). Coupling of an aryl halide (chlorobenzene) and an alkyl halide (chloromethane) with sodium in dry ether is the Wurtz-Fittig reaction, producing toluene (methylbenzene). Thus, $\text{R} \rightarrow 2$.
Step 4: Match reaction (S). Diazotization of aniline followed by Sandmeyer reaction with $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2/\text{HCl}$ converts the diazonium group into a chloro group, yielding chlorobenzene. Thus, $\text{S} \rightarrow 1$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Cyclohexene is treated with $N$-bromosuccinimide (NBS) in carbon tetrachloride ($\text{CCl}_4$) in the presence of light ($h\nu$) and a trace of benzoyl peroxide. What is the major organic product formed and its reaction mechanism?
options: A) 1-Bromocyclohex-1-ene via vinylic radical substitution
B) 1,2-Dibromocyclohexane via electrophilic addition across the double bond
C) 3-Bromocyclohex-1-ene via allylic free-radical bromination
D) Bromocyclohexane via free-radical addition of $\text{HBr}$
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the function of NBS. $N$-Bromosuccinimide (NBS) is a specialized reagent used for selective allylic and benzylic bromination of alkenes and alkylarenes.
Step 2: Trace the free-radical mechanism. Light initiates cleavage of the weak $\text{N}-\text{Br}$ bond in NBS to generate a bromine free radical ($\text{Br}^\bullet$). The bromine radical selectively abstracts an allylic hydrogen atom from cyclohexene because the developing cyclohexenyl radical is strongly stabilized by resonance with the adjacent carbon-carbon double bond (allylic resonance energy $\approx 50\text{ kJ/mol}$).
Step 3: Analyze product formation. NBS maintains a steady, very low concentration of molecular bromine ($\text{Br}_2$) in solution by reacting with trace $\text{HBr}$. The resonance-stabilized allylic radical reacts with $\text{Br}_2$ to yield 3-bromocyclohex-1-ene while regenerating a bromine radical. Electrophilic addition across the double bond is suppressed due to the low $\text{Br}_2$ concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Two isomeric dihaloalkanes with molecular formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Cl}_2$, Compound X and Compound Y, are subjected to alkaline hydrolysis with aqueous potassium hydroxide ($\text{aq. KOH}$):
- Compound X yields an aldehyde (ethanal) as the sole organic product.
- Compound Y yields a diol (ethane-1,2-diol) as the sole organic product.
Which of the following correctly identifies Compound X, Compound Y, and their classification?
options: A) Compound X is 1,1-dichloroethane (vicinal dihalide); Compound Y is 1,2-dichloroethane (geminal dihalide)
B) Compound X is 1,2-dichloroethane (vicinal dihalide); Compound Y is 1,1-dichloroethane (geminal dihalide)
C) Both Compound X and Compound Y are vicinal dihalides
D) Compound X is 1,1-dichloroethane (geminal dihalide); Compound Y is 1,2-dichloroethane (vicinal dihalide)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand geminal vs vicinal dihalides. In geminal dihalides (alkylidene halides), both halogen atoms are attached to the same carbon atom. In vicinal dihalides (alkylene dihalides), the two halogen atoms are attached to adjacent carbon atoms.
Step 2: Analyze hydrolysis of Compound X. In 1,1-dichloroethane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(Cl)}_2$), nucleophilic displacement of both chlorine atoms by hydroxide produces an unstable gem-diol intermediate: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}_2$. Gem-diols spontaneously lose a molecule of water to produce a carbonyl group, yielding ethanal (acetaldehyde, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$). Hence, Compound X is 1,1-dichloroethane (a geminal dihalide).
Step 3: Analyze hydrolysis of Compound Y. In 1,2-dichloroethane ($\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$), nucleophilic displacement of chlorine on each carbon by hydroxide produces a stable vicinal diol: ethane-1,2-diol (ethylene glycol, $\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$). Hence, Compound Y is 1,2-dichloroethane (a vicinal dihalide).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding organometallic reactions of haloalkanes and haloarenes:
Statement I: The reaction of phenylmagnesium bromide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}$) with propan-2-one (acetone) in dry ether followed by acidic hydrolysis produces 2-phenylpropan-2-ol as a tertiary alcohol.
Statement II: Grignard reagents add nucleophilically across the polar carbonyl double bond ($\text{C}^{\delta+}=\text{O}^{\delta-}$), wherein the nucleophilic carbon atom of the alkyl/aryl group attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon while the magnesium atom coordinates to the carbonyl oxygen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. The reaction of a ketone with a Grignard reagent yields a tertiary alcohol upon hydrolysis. Specifically, addition of phenylmagnesium bromide to acetone ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{O}$) produces a magnesium alkoxide adduct ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)-\text{OMgBr}$), which upon acidification with dilute $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ hydrolyzes to 2-phenylpropan-2-ol: $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)\text{OH}$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The carbon-magnesium bond in Grignard reagents is strongly polarized ($C^{\delta-} - \text{Mg}^{\delta+}$). The carbonyl carbon of the ketone is electron-deficient due to electronegativity of oxygen ($C^{\delta+} = \text{O}^{\delta-}$). The nucleophilic aryl/alkyl carbanion attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon, forming a new carbon-carbon bond, while the electropositive $-\text{MgX}$ group coordinates to oxygen to form a halo-magnesium alkoxide complex. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When $(2E)$-but-2-ene and $(2Z)$-but-2-ene are treated separately with bromine in carbon tetrachloride ($\text{Br}_2/\text{CCl}_4$) in the dark, what are the stereochemical configurations of the 2,3-dibromobutane products obtained from the $(E)$ and $(Z)$ isomers, respectively?
options: A) $(2E)$-but-2-ene gives a racemic $(\pm)$-mixture, while $(2Z)$-but-2-ene gives $meso$-2,3-dibromobutane
B) $(2E)$-but-2-ene gives $meso$-2,3-dibromobutane, while $(2Z)$-but-2-ene gives a racemic $(\pm)$-mixture of $(2R,3R)$- and $(2S,3S)$-2,3-dibromobutane
C) Both $(2E)$- and $(2Z)$-but-2-ene yield $meso$-2,3-dibromobutane exclusively
D) Both $(2E)$- and $(2Z)$-but-2-ene yield a racemic $(\pm)$-mixture exclusively
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the stereochemical mechanism of electrophilic bromination of alkenes. The addition of bromine ($\text{Br}_2$) to alkenes is a stereospecific anti-addition proceeding through a cyclic bromonium ion intermediate followed by backside nucleophilic attack of bromide ($\text{Br}^-$).
Step 2: Apply anti-addition to $(E)$-but-2-ene (trans isomer). Anti-addition of two identical halogen atoms across a symmetrical trans alkene ($E$-alkene) creates a molecule with an internal plane of symmetry. Attack of bromide on either carbon of the cyclic bromonium ion produces identical structures that are superimposable on their mirror images, yielding the optically inactive $meso$-2,3-dibromobutane.
Step 3: Apply anti-addition to $(Z)$-but-2-ene (cis isomer). Anti-addition across a symmetrical cis alkene ($Z$-alkene) produces a chiral product lacking any internal symmetry plane. Backside attack on the two bridgehead carbons occurs with equal probability, generating an equimolar ($1:1$) pair of enantiomers: $(2R,3R)$-2,3-dibromobutane and $(2S,3S)$-2,3-dibromobutane (a racemic mixture).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following comprehensive reaction sequence involving haloalkane and polyhalogen chemistry:
$$\text{Ethanol} \xrightarrow{\text{PCl}_5} \text{A} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN (alc.)}} \text{B} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \Delta} \text{C} \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_3, \Delta} \text{D} \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2 / \text{aq. KOH}} \text{E} \xrightarrow{\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{alc. KOH}, \Delta} \text{F}$$
What is the structure and characteristic property of Compound F?
options: A) Ethyl cyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$), an odourless crystalline solid
B) Propyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NC}$), having a fruity ester-like fragrance
C) Ethyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC}$), having an extremely intolerable and foul odour
D) Methyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{NC}$), a sweet-smelling gas
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify Compound A. Reaction of ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) with $\text{PCl}_5$ yields chloroethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$).
Step 2: Identify Compound B and C. Nucleophilic substitution of chloroethane with alcoholic $\text{KCN}$ yields propanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$, Compound B). Complete acidic hydrolysis of the nitrile yields propanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, Compound C).
Step 3: Identify Compound D and E. Reaction of propanoic acid with ammonia followed by strong heating yields propanamide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$, Compound D). Treatment of propanamide with bromine and aqueous $\text{KOH}$ is the Hoffmann bromamide degradation, which degrades the carbon chain by one carbon to produce ethanamine (ethylamine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, Compound E).
Step 4: Identify Compound F. Reaction of primary amine ethanamine with chloroform and alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ is the carbylamine test (isocyanide test): $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 + \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{KOH} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC} + 3\text{KCl} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Compound F is ethyl isocyanide (ethyl carbylamine), famous for its extremely foul and repulsive odor.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the laboratory preparation of alkanes by decarboxylation:
Statement I: Heating sodium ethanoate with soda lime (a mixture of $\text{NaOH}$ and $\text{CaO}$ in a $3:1$ mass ratio) produces methane gas.
Statement II: Soda lime decarboxylation of a sodium carboxylate yields an alkane containing the same number of carbon atoms as the parent carboxylic acid salt.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. Heating sodium ethanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$) with soda lime ($\text{NaOH} + \text{CaO}$ in a $3:1$ mass ratio) eliminates carbon dioxide as sodium carbonate according to the reaction:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + \text{NaOH} \xrightarrow{\text{CaO}, \Delta} \text{CH}_4 + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$$
This produces methane gas, confirming that Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. Decarboxylation eliminates the carboxyl group as carbonate, yielding an alkane that contains one carbon atom less than the starting sodium carboxylate (descent of homologous series). Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.
Step 3: Calcium oxide ($\text{CaO}$) keeps sodium hydroxide dry due to its hygroscopic nature and prevents fusion of glass apparatus at elevated reaction temperatures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Kolbe's electrolytic synthesis cannot be employed for the preparation of methane.
Reason (R): In Kolbe's electrolytic decarboxylation of carboxylate salts, the hydrocarbon is formed at the anode via the coupling of two alkyl free radicals.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). In Kolbe's electrolytic method, an aqueous solution of sodium or potassium salt of a carboxylic acid on electrolysis gives an alkane containing an even number of carbon atoms. The smallest carboxylate salt used is acetate ($\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$), which couples to yield ethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{-}\text{CH}_3$). Methane contains only one carbon atom and cannot be formed by radical dimerization. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). At the anode, acetate ions lose an electron to form acetate radicals, which undergo rapid decarboxylation yielding methyl radicals ($\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$). Two methyl radicals then couple to form ethane:
$$2\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3$$
Because the coupling step fundamentally requires at least two alkyl radicals (yielding at least two carbon atoms), methane cannot be synthesized. Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the conformational analysis of ethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{-}\text{CH}_3$), the dihedral angle between the carbon-hydrogen bonds in the staggered conformation and its relative thermodynamic stability compared to the eclipsed conformation are respectively:
options: A) $0^\circ$ and less stable due to maximum torsional strain
B) $60^\circ$ and more stable due to minimum torsional strain
C) $120^\circ$ and less stable due to angle strain
D) $180^\circ$ and more stable due to absence of steric hindrance
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Define dihedral angle (torsional angle). It represents the angle between the $\text{C-H}$ bonds on adjacent carbon atoms when viewed along the $\text{C-C}$ bond axis (Newman projection).
Step 2: In the staggered conformation of ethane, each $\text{C-H}$ bond on the front carbon bisects the angle between the two $\text{C-H}$ bonds on the rear carbon, making the dihedral angle exactly $60^\circ$.
Step 3: In this staggered arrangement, the electron clouds of the $\text{C-H}$ $\sigma$-bonds are at maximum possible spatial separation, resulting in minimum electron-electron repulsion (minimum torsional strain). Consequently, the staggered conformation is more stable than the eclipsed conformation (dihedral angle $0^\circ$) by approximately $12.55\text{ kJ/mol}$ ($3\text{ kcal/mol}$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the Wurtz reaction:
Statement I: The Wurtz reaction of an equimolar mixture of chloromethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$) and chloroethane ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$) with sodium in dry ether produces exclusively propane.
Statement II: Unsymmetrical alkanes containing an odd number of carbon atoms are generally not prepared in practical yields by the Wurtz reaction because a mixture of three different alkanes is obtained, which are difficult to separate due to close boiling points.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. When two different alkyl halides ($\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$) react with sodium in dry ether, self-coupling as well as cross-coupling occur, producing three distinct alkanes:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{Na/dry ether}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3 \text{ (ethane)} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ (propane)} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ (butane)}$$
Hence, propane is not obtained exclusively. Statement I is incorrect.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. The resulting mixture of homologous alkanes (ethane, propane, and butane) possesses closely spaced boiling points, making separation by fractional distillation extremely difficult and rendering the reaction unsuitable for preparing unsymmetrical alkanes in pure form. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When methane and dioxygen in a $2:1$ volume ratio are passed through a copper tube at $523\text{ K}$ under a pressure of $100\text{ atm}$, the primary organic product obtained is:
options: A) Methanoic acid
B) Methanal
C) Carbon monoxide
D) Methanol
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Recall the conditions for controlled catalytic oxidation of methane as specified in NCERT.
Step 2: Passing a mixture of methane and oxygen through a copper tube at $523\text{ K}$ and $100\text{ atm}$ oxidizes methane selectively to methanol:
$$2\text{CH}_4 + \text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Cu / } 523\text{ K / } 100\text{ atm}} 2\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$$
Step 3: In contrast, oxidation with molybdenum oxide ($\text{Mo}_2\text{O}_3$) catalyst gives methanal ($\text{HCHO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$), while oxidation of higher alkanes with manganese acetate yields carboxylic acids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Heating n-hexane at $773\text{ K}$ and $10\text{--}20\text{ atm}$ in the presence of chromium oxide supported on alumina ($\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3/\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) results in the formation of:
options: A) Cyclohexane
B) Hex-1-ene
C) Benzene
D) 2-Methylpentane
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the chemical transformation described by the specified reagents and conditions.
Step 2: Alkanes containing 6 to 8 carbon atoms on heating to $773\text{ K}$ at $10\text{--}20\text{ atm}$ in the presence of oxides of chromium, vanadium, or molybdenum supported over alumina undergo cyclization followed by dehydrogenation to yield aromatic hydrocarbons. This process is known as aromatization or catalytic reforming.
Step 3: n-Hexane ($\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{CH}_3$) undergoes ring closure with loss of hydrogen to yield benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$):
$$\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3/\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3, \; 773\text{ K}, \; 10\text{-}20\text{ atm}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 4\text{H}_2$$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the halogenation of alkanes:
Statement I: The rate of replacement of hydrogens of alkanes during free radical substitution follows the order: $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$.
Statement II: Halogenation of alkanes with iodine is reversible and slow, requiring the presence of an oxidizing agent such as $\text{HIO}_3$ or $\text{HNO}_3$ to consume the $\text{HI}$ formed.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In free radical halogenation, hydrogen abstraction by a halogen radical generates an alkyl free radical. Since tertiary alkyl radicals are stabilized by hyperconjugation and inductive effects, the stability order is $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$. The bond dissociation enthalpy of the $\text{C-H}$ bond is lowest for $3^\circ$ carbons; thus, the rate of replacement follows $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Iodination is endothermic and reversible:
$$\text{CH}_4 + \text{I}_2 \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{I} + \text{HI}$$
Hydroiodic acid ($\text{HI}$) is a powerful reducing agent that reduces alkyl iodides back to alkanes. Adding an oxidizing agent like iodic acid ($\text{HIO}_3$) or nitric acid ($\text{HNO}_3$) oxidizes $\text{HI}$ to $\text{I}_2$ ($5\text{HI} + \text{HIO}_3 \rightarrow 3\text{I}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$), shifting the equilibrium forward according to Le Chatelier's principle. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding conformations of ethane:

List I (Parameter / Conformation)
A. Dihedral angle in eclipsed form
B. Dihedral angle in staggered form
C. Energy difference between eclipsed and staggered forms
D. Skew conformation

List II (Value / Description)
I. $60^\circ$
II. $0^\circ$
III. Any intermediate conformation with dihedral angle between $0^\circ$ and $60^\circ$
IV. $\approx 12.55\text{ kJ/mol}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
B) A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
C) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
D) A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In the eclipsed conformation of ethane, hydrogen atoms on adjacent carbons are directly aligned, giving a dihedral angle of $0^\circ$ (A matches II).
Step 2: In the staggered conformation, the $\text{C-H}$ bonds are spaced maximally apart with a dihedral angle of $60^\circ$ (B matches I).
Step 3: The magnitude of torsional strain causing the energy difference between the eclipsed and staggered forms of ethane is approximately $12.55\text{ kJ/mol}$ or $3.0\text{ kcal/mol}$ (C matches IV).
Step 4: Any infinite intermediate arrangement between the fully eclipsed and staggered conformations is designated as a skew conformation (D matches III).
Hence, the correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Which of the following alkenes exhibits geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism?
options: A) Propene
B) But-2-ene
C) But-1-ene
D) 2-Methylpropene
questions.explanation:
Step 1: State the requirement for geometrical isomerism in alkenes: restricted rotation about the $\text{C=C}$ double bond, and each of the doubly bonded carbon atoms must be attached to two different atoms or groups (i.e. $\text{abC=Cab}$ or $\text{abC=Ccd}$).
Step 2: In propene ($\text{CH}_2\text{=CH-CH}_3$), but-1-ene ($\text{CH}_2\text{=CH-CH}_2\text{CH}_3$), and 2-methylpropene ($\text{CH}_2\text{=C(CH}_3)_2$), one of the sp2 carbons is bonded to two identical hydrogen atoms. Therefore, swapping groups does not yield a stereoisomer.
Step 3: In but-2-ene ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_3$), each sp2 carbon is bonded to $-\text{H}$ and $-\text{CH}_3$ (two distinct groups). Consequently, it exists as two distinct geometrical isomers: cis-but-2-ene (methyl groups on the same side) and trans-but-2-ene (methyl groups on opposite sides).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the stereoselective reduction of alkynes to alkenes:
Statement I: Controlled catalytic hydrogenation of but-2-yne using Lindlar's catalyst (palladised charcoal partially deactivated with quinoline or sulfur) yields cis-but-2-ene.
Statement II: Reduction of but-2-yne with sodium in liquid ammonia (Birch reduction) yields trans-but-2-ene.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Lindlar's catalyst is palladium supported on calcium carbonate or barium sulfate poisoned with quinoline or lead salts. The adsorption of the alkyne onto the metal surface allows dihydrogen to add from the same face (syn-addition), yielding predominantly the cis-alkene (cis-but-2-ene). Poisoning prevents over-reduction to the alkane. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Reduction with sodium in liquid ammonia proceeds via single electron transfer and radical-anion intermediates, where the trans-configuration of the vinyl radical anion is thermodynamically favored due to minimum electrostatic and steric repulsion. Protonation results in anti-addition, forming the trans-alkene (trans-but-2-ene). Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Electrophilic addition of hydrogen bromide ($\text{HBr}$) to propene in the absence of peroxides gives 2-bromopropane as the major product.
Reason (R): The addition proceeds via the formation of a secondary carbocation ($\text{CH}_3\text{-}\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H-CH}_3$), which is more stable than a primary carbocation ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$).
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). According to Markovnikov's rule, when an unsymmetrical reagent adds to an unsymmetrical alkene, the negative part of the addendum attaches to the double-bonded carbon having fewer hydrogen atoms. Thus, addition of $\text{HBr}$ to propene yields 2-bromopropane as the major product. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). The mechanism involves initial electrophilic attack by $\text{H}^+$. Attack at $\text{C-1}$ produces a secondary carbocation ($\text{CH}_3\text{-}\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H-CH}_3$) stabilized by 6 hyperconjugative hydrogens, while attack at $\text{C-2}$ produces a primary carbocation ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$) stabilized by only 2 hyperconjugative hydrogens. Rapid nucleophilic capture of the secondary carbocation by $\text{Br}^-$ yields 2-bromopropane. Thus, Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the Kharasch (peroxide) effect:
Statement I: Addition of $\text{HBr}$ to unsymmetrical alkenes in the presence of benzoyl peroxide yields anti-Markovnikov products via a free radical pathway.
Statement II: The peroxide effect is readily observed with $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HI}$ under identical reaction conditions.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. In the presence of organic peroxides, addition of $\text{HBr}$ to unsymmetrical alkenes occurs contrary to Markovnikov's rule (Kharasch effect) through a free radical chain mechanism where $\text{Br}^\bullet$ adds first to generate the more stable free radical. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. The $\text{H-Cl}$ bond is strong ($430.5\text{ kJ/mol}$) and is not cleaved homolytically by the alkoxy radical. Conversely, although the $\text{H-I}$ bond is weak ($296.8\text{ kJ/mol}$) and forms iodine radicals readily, the addition of $\text{I}^\bullet$ to a double bond is endothermic; instead, iodine radicals combine with each other to regenerate $\text{I}_2$. Hence, the peroxide effect is observed exclusively with $\text{HBr}$ and not with $\text{HCl}$ or $\text{HI}$. Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Treatment of propene with cold, dilute, alkaline potassium permanganate solution (Baeyer's reagent) yields which of the following compounds as the major product?
options: A) Propanoic acid
B) Propan-2-one and methanoic acid
C) Propan-1-ol
D) Propane-1,2-diol
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify Baeyer's reagent. Baeyer's reagent is a cold, dilute ($1\%$) aqueous alkaline solution of potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$).
Step 2: Alkenes react with Baeyer's reagent at room temperature to undergo syn-dihydroxylation across the double bond, converting the alkene into a vicinal glycol.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + [\text{O}] \xrightarrow{\text{dil. alkaline KMnO}_4, \; 273\text{--}283\text{ K}} \text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-CH}_2\text{OH}$$
Step 3: The purple color of permanganate is discharged with the precipitation of brown manganese dioxide ($\text{MnO}_2$), serving as a qualitative test for unsaturation. The product formed from propene is propane-1,2-diol (propylene glycol).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: An alkene on reductive ozonolysis with $\text{O}_3$ followed by cleavage with $\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$ yields an equimolar mixture of propan-2-one (acetone) and ethanal (acetaldehyde). The IUPAC name of the alkene is:
options: A) 2-Methylbut-1-ene
B) 2-Methylbut-2-ene
C) Pent-2-ene
D) 3-Methylbut-1-ene
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Write down the structures of the carbonyl cleavage products:
Propan-2-one: $\text{CH}_3\text{-C}(=\text{O})\text{-CH}_3$
Ethanal: $\text{O=CH-CH}_3$
Step 2: To deduce the structure of the starting alkene, remove the oxygen atoms from both carbonyl groups and join the two fragments via a carbon-carbon double bond:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{-C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{=CH-CH}_3$$
Step 3: Number the carbon chain according to IUPAC nomenclature from the end closer to the branch: the longest continuous chain contains 4 carbon atoms with a double bond at carbon-2 and a methyl substituent at carbon-2. Therefore, the IUPAC name is 2-methylbut-2-ene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromobutane with alcoholic potassium hydroxide ($\text{alc. } \text{KOH}$) predominantly produces but-2-ene rather than but-1-ene.
Reason (R): According to Saytzeff's rule, in $\beta$-elimination reactions, the alkene possessing the lesser number of alkyl substituents attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms is the preferred (major) product.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Heating 2-bromobutane with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ undergoes an E2 dehydrohalogenation. The base can abstract a $\beta$-hydrogen from $\text{C-1}$ to give but-1-ene ($19\%$) or from $\text{C-3}$ to give but-2-ene ($81\%$). Thus, but-2-ene is the major product, and Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Saytzeff's rule explicitly states that elimination proceeds preferentially to yield the alkene that has the greater number of alkyl substituents attached to the doubly bonded carbons (more substituted alkene is more stable due to hyperconjugation). The Reason mistakenly claims that the lesser substituted alkene is favored. Thus, Reason (R) is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the acidity of hydrocarbons:
Statement I: Ethyne is significantly more acidic than ethene and ethane because its carbon atoms are sp hybridized with $50\%$ s-character, making them strongly electronegative.
Statement II: Ethyne reacts with sodamide ($\text{NaNH}_2$) in liquid ammonia to produce sodium acetylide and liberate ammonia gas.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. The hybridization of carbon atoms in ethyne, ethene, and ethane is $\text{sp}$ ($50\%$ s-character), $\text{sp}^2$ ($33.3\%$ s-character), and $\text{sp}^3$ ($25\%$ s-character), respectively. Electrons in s-orbitals are closer to the atomic nucleus; hence, higher s-character leads to greater electronegativity of the carbon atom. The $\text{C-H}$ bond in ethyne is strongly polarized, allowing terminal protons to be released to strong bases. The acidity order is $\text{HC}\equiv\text{CH} > \text{CH}_2\text{=CH}_2 > \text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_3$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. Sodamide ($\text{NaNH}_2$) is the conjugate base of ammonia ($pK_a \approx 38$). Since ethyne ($pK_a \approx 25$) is a stronger acid than ammonia, the amide ion ($\text{NH}_2^-$) deprotonates ethyne to form sodium acetylide ($\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}^-\text{Na}^+$) and ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$). Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: When propyne ($\text{CH}_3\text{-C}\equiv\text{CH}$) is warmed with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the presence of $\text{HgSO}_4$ catalyst at $333\text{ K}$, the major stable product isolated is:
options: A) Propanal
B) Propan-1-ol
C) Propanoic acid
D) Propan-2-one
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the reaction. Acid-catalyzed hydration of alkynes in the presence of mercuric sulfate ($\text{HgSO}_4$) at $333\text{ K}$ proceeds via electrophilic addition of water across the triple bond.
Step 2: For propyne (an unsymmetrical alkyne), addition of water follows Markovnikov's rule. The $\text{H}^+$ attaches to the terminal $\text{CH}$ carbon, and $-\text{OH}$ attaches to the central carbon ($\text{C-2}$), forming the unstable enol intermediate prop-1-en-2-ol:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{-C}\equiv\text{CH} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 / \text{HgSO}_4, \; 333\text{ K}} [\text{CH}_3\text{-C(OH)=CH}_2]$$
Step 3: The enol intermediate rapidly tautomerizes into the thermodynamically favored keto form, yielding propan-2-one (acetone):
$$[\text{CH}_3\text{-C(OH)=CH}_2] \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{-CO-CH}_3$$
Step 4: Note that ethyne is the only alkyne that yields an aldehyde (ethanal) under these hydration conditions; all higher terminal and internal alkynes yield ketones.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Passing ethyne gas through a red hot iron tube at $873\text{ K}$ leads to its cyclic polymerization, forming:
options: A) Cyclohexane
B) Benzene
C) Toluene
D) Mesitylene
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Recall the cyclic polymerization reaction of alkynes as described in NCERT Class 11 Chemistry.
Step 2: When ethyne (acetylene) gas is passed through a red hot iron or copper tube at $873\text{ K}$, three molecules of ethyne undergo cyclic trimerization to form benzene:
$$3\text{C}_2\text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Red hot iron tube, } 873\text{ K}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6$$
Step 3: This reaction represents an important synthetic entry route from aliphatic hydrocarbons to aromatic compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding aromaticity and $(4n+2)\pi$ electron counts:

List I (Species)
A. Benzene
B. Cyclopentadienyl anion
C. Tropylium cation (cycloheptatrienyl cation)
D. Cyclooctatetraene

List II (Aromatic character / Delocalized $\pi$-electrons)
I. Aromatic ($6\pi$-electrons, $n=1$)
II. Non-aromatic ($8\pi$-electrons, adopts non-planar tub conformation)
III. Aromatic ($6\pi$-electrons with a carbanionic center, $n=1$)
IV. Aromatic ($6\pi$-electrons with a planar carbocationic 7-membered ring, $n=1$)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
B) A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
C) A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
D) A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Benzene is a planar, completely conjugated cyclic hydrocarbon containing $6\pi$ electrons ($n=1$), making it classic aromatic (A matches I).
Step 2: Cyclopentadienyl anion contains a 5-membered conjugated planar ring with 4 electrons from two double bonds plus 2 electrons from the lone pair on the carbanion carbon, giving $6\pi$ electrons ($n=1$) and aromaticity (B matches III).
Step 3: Tropylium cation is a planar 7-membered cyclic system containing 3 conjugated double bonds with an empty p-orbital on the carbocation carbon, having $6\pi$ electrons ($n=1$) and exceptional aromatic stability (C matches IV).
Step 4: Cyclooctatetraene has $8\pi$ electrons. If planar, it would be an antiaromatic $4n\pi$ system; to escape antiaromatic destabilization, it distorts into a non-planar tub-shaped geometry, rendering it non-aromatic (D matches II).
Hence, the correct match is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In the nitration of benzene using a mixture of concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, nitric acid acts as a Brønsted-Lowry base.
Reason (R): Concentrated sulfuric acid is a stronger acid than concentrated nitric acid and protonates $\text{HNO}_3$ to generate the nitronium ion ($\text{NO}_2^+$).
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). In the nitrating mixture, concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ donates a proton to concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$:
$$\text{HNO}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightleftharpoons \text{NO}_2^+ + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+ + 2\text{HSO}_4^-$$
Because $\text{HNO}_3$ accepts a proton, it functions as a Brønsted-Lowry base. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Sulfuric acid has a much higher acid dissociation constant than nitric acid. Protonation of the hydroxyl oxygen of $\text{HNO}_3$ gives the protonated species ($\text{H}_2\text{O}^+\text{-NO}_2$), which spontaneously loses water to generate the electrophile nitronium ion ($\text{NO}_2^+$). Thus, Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the directive influence of functional groups attached to a benzene ring:
Statement I: The hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$) in phenol is activating and directs incoming electrophiles predominantly to the ortho and para positions due to the $+M$ resonance effect.
Statement II: The nitro group ($-\text{NO}_2$) in nitrobenzene is deactivating and directs incoming electrophiles to the meta position due to its $-M$ and $-I$ electron-withdrawing effects.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. The oxygen atom of the $-\text{OH}$ group possesses lone pairs that delocalize into the aromatic $\pi$-system via the positive resonance ($+M$) effect. Resonance structures reveal that electron density increases specifically at the ortho and para positions relative to the meta positions. Therefore, $-\text{OH}$ activates the ring and directs electrophilic attack to ortho and para positions. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. The nitrogen atom in $-\text{NO}_2$ bears a formal positive charge and is bonded to electronegative oxygens, exerting strong $-M$ and $-I$ electron withdrawal. Resonance delocalization places formal positive charges on the ortho and para carbons, heavily destabilizing electrophilic attack at those sites. The meta position is comparatively less electron-deficient, directing electrophiles to the meta position. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with chloromethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$) in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride ($\text{AlCl}_3$), the primary role of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is to:
options: A) Act as a Brønsted-Lowry base to abstract a proton from the Arenium ion
B) Act as an oxidizing agent to convert toluene to benzoic acid
C) Act as a Lewis acid to generate the electrophilic methyl cation species from chloromethane
D) Act as a free radical initiator to initiate homolytic cleavage of the carbon-chlorine bond
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the mechanism of Friedel-Crafts alkylation.
Step 2: Anhydrous aluminium chloride ($\text{AlCl}_3$) is an electron-deficient compound with an incomplete octet on aluminium (6 valence electrons), acting as a powerful Lewis acid.
Step 3: $\text{AlCl}_3$ coordinates with the lone pair of chlorine in chloromethane to form a polarized complex or methyl cation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{AlCl}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3^{\delta+} \dots \text{Cl} \dots \text{AlCl}_3^{\delta-} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3^+ + [\text{AlCl}_4]^-$$
Step 4: This generates the electrophilic methyl carbocation species, which attacks the benzene ring to initiate electrophilic aromatic substitution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the products of Kolbe's electrolytic synthesis:
Statement I: Electrolysis of a concentrated aqueous solution of sodium propanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa}$) yields n-butane as the major coupling product at the anode.
Statement II: In addition to n-butane, disproportionation of intermediate ethyl radicals at the anode yields small amounts of ethane and ethene.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. During electrolysis of aqueous sodium propanoate, propanoate ions migrate to the anode, lose one electron, and decarboxylate to generate ethyl free radicals ($\text{CH}_3\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$). Two ethyl radicals undergo radical-radical dimerization to yield n-butane as the principal product:
$$2\text{CH}_3\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. Alongside symmetrical coupling, two ethyl free radicals can participate in a competing disproportionation pathway, wherein one radical abstracts a $\beta$-hydrogen from another:
$$\text{CH}_3\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 + \text{CH}_3\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3 \text{ (ethane)} + \text{CH}_2\text{=CH}_2 \text{ (ethene)}$$
Consequently, minor quantities of ethane and ethene are detected at the anode. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Among the structural isomers of pentane ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}$), 2,2-dimethylpropane (neopentane) has a lower boiling point ($282.5\text{ K}$) than n-pentane ($309\text{ K}$), yet its melting point ($256.4\text{ K}$) is significantly higher than that of n-pentane ($143.3\text{ K}$).
Reason (R): Branching causes neopentane to adopt an almost spherical shape with a smaller surface area, decreasing intermolecular van der Waals forces, while its high spherical symmetry allows it to pack more compactly into a crystal lattice.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). As documented in NCERT, isomeric pentanes exhibit the boiling point order: n-pentane ($309\text{ K}$) > isopentane ($301\text{ K}$) > neopentane ($282.5\text{ K}$). Conversely, the melting point of neopentane ($256.4\text{ K}$) is substantially higher than that of n-pentane ($143.3\text{ K}$). Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Boiling points depend on intermolecular attractive forces in the liquid state. The spherical geometry of neopentane minimizes surface area, diminishing contact area and London dispersion forces, which reduces its boiling point. In contrast, melting points depend on crystal lattice stability. The highly symmetrical, tetrahedral shape of neopentane fits tightly into the crystal lattice, requiring a higher temperature to break the crystalline solid. Thus, Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Photochemical monobromination of 2-methylpropane gives 2-bromo-2-methylpropane as the almost exclusive product ($>99\%$), whereas photochemical monochlorination produces 1-chloro-2-methylpropane as the major product ($\approx 64\%$).
Reason (R): Bromine free radicals are much more reactive than chlorine free radicals and abstract hydrogen atoms indiscriminately, while chlorine free radicals are sluggish and highly selective.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). 2-Methylpropane possesses nine $1^\circ$ hydrogens and one $3^\circ$ hydrogen. For chlorination, relative reactivity is $1^\circ : 2^\circ : 3^\circ = 1 : 3.8 : 5.0$. The statistical yield of $1^\circ$ alkyl chloride is $9 \times 1 = 9$ versus $1 \times 5 = 5$ for $3^\circ$ chloride, giving $\approx 64\%$ 1-chloro-2-methylpropane. For bromination, relative reactivity is $1 : 82 : 1600$. The yield of $3^\circ$ bromide is $1600 / (1600 + 9) > 99\%$. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). The first propagation step for bromination is endothermic, rendering bromine radicals less reactive and exceptionally selective according to the Hammond postulate. Conversely, hydrogen abstraction by chlorine radicals is exothermic, making chlorine radicals highly reactive and relatively unselective. Reason (R) incorrectly reverses their relative reactivity and selectivity; hence, Reason (R) is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding conformations of butane viewed along the $\text{C}_2\text{-C}_3$ bond:

List I (Conformation)
A. Anti-periplanar conformation
B. Gauche conformation
C. Partially eclipsed conformation
D. Fully eclipsed conformation

List II (Characteristics / Dihedral Angle)
I. Dihedral angle $60^\circ$, displays steric strain (gauche interaction) between adjacent methyl groups
II. Dihedral angle $180^\circ$, minimum potential energy and maximum thermodynamic stability
III. Dihedral angle $0^\circ$, methyl groups eclipse each other with maximum steric and torsional strain
IV. Dihedral angle $120^\circ$, methyl groups eclipse hydrogen atoms with intermediate potential energy

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
B) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
C) A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
D) A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In the anti-periplanar conformation of butane, the two bulky methyl groups are located at an angle of $180^\circ$ to each other, minimizing dipole, torsional, and steric repulsions, resulting in the lowest energy conformation (A matches II).
Step 2: In the gauche conformation, the two methyl groups have a dihedral angle of $60^\circ$. While free of torsional strain, they experience mild steric repulsion (gauche interaction) of approximately $3.8\text{ kJ/mol}$ (B matches I).
Step 3: In the partially eclipsed conformation (dihedral angle $120^\circ$), methyl groups eclipse hydrogen atoms, generating torsional and steric strain (C matches IV).
Step 4: In the fully eclipsed conformation (dihedral angle $0^\circ$), the two methyl groups directly overlap, producing the highest torsional and steric repulsions with maximum potential energy (D matches III).
Hence, the correct match is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.subject: Chemistry
